verdict.rationale: Clerk documents its own open-source migration tool that bulk-creates users in Clerk from a JSON or CSV file via the Backend API and respects rate limits. It also documents a 'Basic Export / Import' strategy and trickle migration for moving into Clerk. The evidence never says password hashes can be imported, and nothing shows exporting users back out of Clerk, which is the anti-lock-in half of the story. missing for 10: documented import of password hashes, documented export of users and hashes out of Clerk, independent or hands-on corroboration of the migration tool.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bulk-import existing users — including password hashes — and export them again, so I am never locked in

citations.quote: Clerk provides an open-source tool that takes a JSON or CSV file as input, containing a list of users, and creates a user in Clerk using the Backend API... The tool respects the backend rate limits.
There are typically two main strategies for migrating your existing user management from a different platform into Clerk: Basic Export / Import, Trickle migration
